title: What training do credit intermediaries need in Portugal?
description: What Decreto-Lei n.º 81-C/2017 requires of credit intermediaries in Portugal: the nine subjects, certification routes, Banco de Portugal role and fines.
shortAnswer: In Portugal, Decreto-Lei n.º 81-C/2017 requires anyone authorized by the Banco de Portugal as a credit intermediary to master nine subjects, from credit products and consumer law to creditworthiness assessment and ethics. Individuals qualify through mandatory schooling plus professional certification from a Banco de Portugal certified training entity, or a qualifying higher or post-secondary diploma. Intermediaries handling housing credit must also assign only competent workers. The regime applied from January 1, 2018.
keyTakeaways: Article 13 of the regime annexed to Decreto-Lei n.º 81-C/2017 lists the nine subjects that count as adequate knowledge and competence for credit intermediaries.

Two routes satisfy the requirement: mandatory schooling plus professional certification in credit intermediation, or a degree or post-secondary diploma whose curriculum covers the minimum training content set by ministerial order (portaria).
Certification training must be delivered by an entity recognized in the National Qualifications System and certified by the Banco de Portugal, which publishes the list of certified entities.
A transitional route based on three years of relevant experience ended on March 21, 2019.

Assigning workers without adequate knowledge to housing credit intermediation is an administrative offense punishable with fines of 750 to 50,000 euros for individuals and 1,500 to 250,000 euros for companies.
appliesTo: Natural and legal persons seeking Banco de Portugal authorization as credit intermediaries or to provide credit advisory services in Portugal
Members of the management body of credit intermediaries that are companies
Technical managers (responsáveis técnicos) designated by intermediaries that do not work on housing credit
Workers of intermediaries who carry out intermediation or advice on housing credit agreements
Workers of creditors marketing housing credit, under the parallel rule in Decreto-Lei n.º 74-A/2017

sections.heading: Which law sets the training rules for credit intermediaries in Portugal?

blocks.text: The rules are in the legal regime annexed to Decreto-Lei n.º 81-C/2017, of July 7, which governs access to and exercise of the activity of credit intermediary and the provision of credit advisory services. It transposed the intermediary provisions of the EU [Mortgage Credit Directive](/regulations/mortgage-credit-directive-staff-knowledge-competence) and applies to all credit agreements an intermediary handles, not only mortgages. The decree entered into force on January 1, 2018 ([Diário da República, 1.ª série, n.º 130](https://dre.pt/application/conteudo/107648947)).

The Banco de Portugal authorizes and registers intermediaries and supervises the regime. Article 4 of the decree required the implementing ministerial orders and any Banco de Portugal notices (avisos) to be published within 90 days, and Article 5 required the Banco de Portugal to publish an impact assessment report at the end of 2019. This page describes the regime as published in 2017. Readers should check the consolidated version in the Diário da República for later amendments as at November 2026.

Creditors' own staff are covered separately. Article 6 of Decreto-Lei n.º 74-A/2017, of June 23, which transposed the rest of the Mortgage Credit Directive, requires lenders with a head office or branch in Portugal to ensure their workers possess and keep up to date adequate knowledge for housing credit ([Diário da República, 1.ª série, n.º 120](https://dre.pt/application/conteudo/107561581)).

sections.heading: What must a credit intermediary know?

blocks.text: Article 13(1) of the regime defines adequate knowledge and competence as command of nine subjects. Two of them apply only to intermediaries working on housing credit, and the register subject switches to movable property registers for other credit.

blocks.caption: The nine subjects in Article 13(1), Decreto-Lei n.º 81-C/2017
head: Point
Subject
Scope
rows: Characteristics of the credit products marketed and the ancillary services usually offered with them
Legislation applicable to credit agreements, especially consumer protection
Valuation of the guarantees usually required for credit
Organization and functioning of property registers, or of registrable movable property registers in other cases
Real estate registers for housing credit, movable registers otherwise
Fundamental notions of economics and finance

blocks.text: The list closely tracks Annex III of the Directive, with one difference: the Portuguese text refers to the credit market in Portugal in general, while Article 6(2)(f) of Decreto-Lei n.º 74-A/2017 refers specifically to the mortgage credit market for creditor staff.

sections.heading: How does a person prove adequate knowledge and competence?

blocks.text: A natural person qualifies by one of two routes in Article 13(2): completing mandatory schooling and holding professional certification in credit intermediation, or holding an academic degree, a higher professional technician diploma or a post-secondary diploma whose study plan includes the minimum training content. In both routes the minimum content is defined by a joint ministerial order (portaria) of the members of Government responsible for finance, higher education, education and vocational training, which may set role specific content (Article 13(4)).

items: **Who delivers certification training:** a training entity recognized within the National Qualifications System (Sistema Nacional de Qualificações), under Article 13(5).
**Who certifies the training entity:** the Banco de Portugal, under a certification regime approved by ministerial order (Article 13(6)).
**Where to check:** the Banco de Portugal publishes the list of certified training entities on its website (Article 13(7)).
**Foreign qualifications:** qualifications obtained in another EU or EEA Member State are recognized by the Banco de Portugal under Lei n.º 9/2009 (Article 13(8)).

blocks.text: Article 13(3) provided a transitional route: until March 21, 2019, people who had worked for at least three years, consecutively or not, as a credit intermediary, a director or technical manager of one, a creditor employee directly involved in granting credit, or an intermediary employee directly involved in intermediation were treated as competent. That route has closed, so new entrants must qualify through certification or a qualifying diploma.

sections.heading: Who inside an intermediary must meet the requirement?

blocks.text: Who must qualify depends on whether the intermediary is a person or a company and whether it works on housing credit. Article 11 makes adequate knowledge a condition of authorization, and Article 49(2)(b) makes it a continuing conduct duty for housing credit work.

items: **Individual intermediaries:** the applicant personally must meet Article 13 (Article 11(2)(f)).
**Companies:** the members of the management body must meet Article 13 (Article 11(3)(d)(ii)).

**Housing credit:** an applicant intending to intermediate or advise on housing credit must ensure its workers have adequate knowledge (Article 11(5)), and an authorized intermediary must assign only such workers to that activity (Article 49(2)(b)).

**Other credit only:** where no housing credit work is planned, the individual and management body requirements are met by designating at least one technical manager (responsável técnico) who meets Article 13 (Article 11(6)).
**Advisory services:** creditors and intermediaries providing advice on housing credit must assign workers with adequate knowledge to that service (Article 66(1)(f)).

blocks.text: Article 6 of the regime recognizes three categories of intermediary: tied (vinculado), ancillary (a título acessório) and independent (não vinculado). Under Article 18 only companies can operate as independent intermediaries. The knowledge requirement applies across all three categories.

sections.heading: What are the penalties for using unqualified staff?

blocks.text: Assigning workers who lack adequate knowledge and competence to housing credit intermediation is a listed administrative offense (contraordenação) under Article 71, point v), of the regime. Article 71 sets fines of 750 to 50,000 euros where the offender is a natural person and 1,500 to 250,000 euros where it is a legal person, in the decree as published in 2017.

For creditors, Article 29(b) of Decreto-Lei n.º 74-A/2017 makes failure to ensure that workers possess and keep up to date adequate knowledge and competence an offense punishable under Article 210(m) of the General Regime for Credit Institutions and Financial Companies (RGICSF). Portugal's broader financial crime training duties are covered in [AML training requirements in Portugal](/regulations/portugal-aml-law-training-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents the nine Article 13 subjects, the housing credit only subjects and each role's scope as a structured framework, with assessment points linked to each subject. Training providers and intermediaries can then show the Banco de Portugal exactly which subjects a certification covers and which workers are cleared for housing credit files.

faqs.q: Can experience alone still qualify someone as a credit intermediary in Portugal?
faqs.a: No. Article 13(3) of the regime treated three years of relevant experience as sufficient only until March 21, 2019. After that date, a person must hold professional certification after mandatory schooling or a qualifying degree or post-secondary diploma covering the minimum training content.

faqs.q: Who can deliver credit intermediary certification training?
faqs.a: Only a training entity recognized within the National Qualifications System and certified by the Banco de Portugal under the ministerial certification regime. Article 13(7) requires the Banco de Portugal to publish the list of certified training entities on its website, so firms should check that list before enrolling staff.

faqs.q: Does every employee of a credit intermediary need certification?
faqs.a: Not in every case. For housing credit work, every worker assigned to intermediation or advice must have adequate knowledge. Where an intermediary does not work on housing credit, the requirement can be met by designating at least one qualified technical manager, alongside the individual or management body requirements.

faqs.q: Do bank employees selling mortgages fall under Decreto-Lei n.º 81-C/2017?
faqs.a: Bank staff selling the bank's own housing credit are covered by Article 6 of Decreto-Lei n.º 74-A/2017, which sets the same nine subjects and similar qualification routes for creditor workers. Decreto-Lei n.º 81-C/2017 governs credit intermediaries and advisory services.
